summary: Backend testing of Prompt-3 admin/supervisor role system. 23/23 new tests pass; full regression of prompt-1 (movement log, 27) and prompt-2 (last-edited popup, 17) also passes — 67/67 total. Verified: migrate_legacy_roles idempotency + admin-row protection (set role='viewer' on admin then re-run migration → admin restored), /me endpoint (401 no header, 401 invalid id, 200 valid supervisor, 403 unapproved, 403 disabled, password_hash never returned), admin-only gating on approve/reject/toggle-active/role/delete (401 unauth, 403 supervisor, 200 admin, 404 missing), /role validation (random→400, viewer→supervisor alias, admin/supervisor accept), shared data endpoints accessible to supervisors (users list, audit-logs/search, reco-adjustments GET), full e2e supervisor→admin promotion grants live approve powers without re-login, default admin cannot be deleted (400).

minor.issue: Endpoint returns 404 when role update has modified_count==0. Setting the same role twice (e.g. setting 'viewer' on an already-supervisor user) yields 404 'User not found' even though the user exists. Should use matched_count instead of modified_count, or return 200 idempotently. Minor cosmetic — currently masked because admin UI only allows toggling between admin/supervisor, not re-applying same role.

action_items: Optional: change PUT /users/{id}/role to use matched_count instead of modified_count so re-applying the same role doesn't return 404. Cosmetic only — no functional impact since FE never re-applies same role.
Optional: align validation error message text. Currently: "Role must be 'admin' or 'supervisor'" — message is clear and acceptable as-is.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_middleware.py is clean, well-documented, and correctly idempotent. Migration silently swallows all exceptions (`except Exception: pass`) to keep startup resilient — acceptable for migration but consider adding a logger.warning() so silent failures are detectable in prod.
audit_routes.py role endpoint correctly treats legacy 'viewer' as supervisor alias before validation — good backwards-compat.

/users (list) endpoint has NO auth gate — any client can list users (without password_hash). If this is intentional (FE needs it pre-login for register/reset flows) document it; otherwise consider get_current_user gate.
audit-logs/search and reco-adjustments are intentionally ungated (data-access endpoints for both roles) — consistent with prompt spec.
test_credentials: admin / admin123 (read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Supervisor users are auto-created and torn down per-test using TEST_ prefix.
seed_data_creation: All test users are created with username prefix TEST_ and deleted in fixture teardown. Migration test temporarily inserts a TEST_mig_<uuid> user with no role field and deletes it after assertion. Default admin role is briefly set to 'viewer' then restored by migrate_legacy_roles within the same test (verified restored before the test exits).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_role_system.py is a clean regression suite for the role system. Run with: `cd /app && source backend/.env && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_role_system.py -v`. Tests are fully self-contained (create+approve+delete their own users via admin headers). Test report XMLs in /app/test_reports/pytest/. Prompt-1 (test_audit_movement_log.py — 27 tests) and prompt-2 (test_last_edited_popup_backend.py — 17 tests) also pass cleanly against the current backend.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. One cosmetic minor: role endpoint uses modified_count to detect missing user → false 404 when re-applying same role. Existing behavior, not regression.
